skill.name: scientific-slides
skill.description: Create structured scientific presentations for conferences, seminars, defenses, and research talks in PowerPoint, PDF, or LaTeX Beamer.
skill.summary: Plan, build, validate, and rehearse scientific slide decks for research audiences.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: No malicious intent, prompt injection, or covert command execution was found. Most static alerts are documentation or syntax false positives. Confirmed risks involve third-party uploads, broad .env discovery, and API-key exposure in process arguments.

remediation.issue: Research figures can be uploaded to OpenRouter without a dedicated consent checkpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before every attachment upload and warn users not to send confidential, unpublished, regulated, or proprietary material.

remediation.issue: The wrapper places the OpenRouter API key in a child process argument.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the --api-key child argument and let the child read OPENROUTER_API_KEY from its inherited environment.

remediation.issue: The dotenv loader searches multiple working and package ancestor directories.
remediation.suggestion: Load only an explicitly selected project .env file, and do not search parent directories automatically.

- Avoid for body text in presentations
- ❌ Avoid italics (hard to read from distance)
- ❌ Avoid clipart or cartoonish graphics (unless appropriate)
- Fix: Simple, solid colors or subtle gradients

content.value_statement: Scientific talks often overload audiences with dense text and poor pacing. This skill structures, designs, and validates clear PowerPoint, PDF, or Beamer presentations.
actual_capabilities: Structures decks for conferences, seminars, thesis defenses, grant pitches, and journal clubs.
Provides Beamer templates for conference talks, academic seminars, and dissertation defenses.
Generates slide images or standalone visuals through OpenRouter with optional reference attachments.
Combines slide images into PDFs and converts PDFs into review images.
Validates slide counts, timing ranges, dimensions, font sizes, and Beamer compilation.
Provides guidance for visual design, data presentation, accessibility, rehearsal, and timing.
limitations: AI image generation requires an OpenRouter key, network access, compatible models, and possible usage charges.
Prompts and attached figures are sent to a third-party service.
Native PowerPoint creation depends on companion PPTX tools that are not bundled here.
Image-based PDF slides are less editable than native PowerPoint or Beamer slides.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Conference Talk
use_cases.description: Turn selected findings into a focused deck with clear timing, citations, and presentation-ready visuals.
use_cases.target_user: Researcher presenting a short conference talk

use_cases.title: Build a Thesis Defense
use_cases.description: Organize dissertation work into a complete narrative with methods, results, implications, and backup slides.

use_cases.title: Teach a Scientific Seminar
use_cases.description: Develop a longer educational presentation with accessible figures, progressive explanations, and rehearsal checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Short Talk
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a {duration}-minute conference deck about {topic} for {audience}. Give slide titles, timing, one message, and one visual per slide.

prompt_templates.title: Transform a Paper
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn my paper on {topic} into a seminar deck. Prioritize {findings}, simplify methods, place citations, and suggest accessible visuals.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Defense
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a {duration}-minute thesis defense from {materials}. Include narrative sections, timing checkpoints, backup slides, and PowerPoint or Beamer implementation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Graduate student preparing a formal defense

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Review {presentation_file} for structure, timing, readability, contrast, overflow, and visual consistency. Produce prioritized corrections and a final validation checklist.

output_examples.input: Plan a 15-minute conference talk about a new diagnostic model.
output: Opening problem and clinical impact, 60 seconds.
Methods overview with one pipeline diagram, 2 minutes.
Three results slides with direct labels, 7 minutes.
Limitations, implications, and closing message, 3 minutes.

output_examples.input: Review a 45-minute thesis defense for timing and readability.
output: Reduce the background section by three slides.
Enlarge axis labels on slides 18 and 21.
Move detailed sensitivity analyses to backup slides.
Reserve five minutes for conclusions and transition buffer.

output_examples.input: Create a Beamer seminar structure for a mathematical research talk.
output: Use the seminar template with a 16:9 layout.
Introduce notation before the first main equation.
Split long derivations across progressive slides.
End with contributions, limitations, and open questions.

best_practices: Confirm the audience, duration, file format, and core message before designing slides.
Attach only approved, non-confidential figures and disclose third-party processing.
Render every slide and review it at a realistic projection size before delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not upload unpublished or confidential figures without explicit authorization.
Do not copy dense paper text directly onto slides.
Do not accept generated citations, labels, or scientific diagrams without verification.

faq.question: Which presentation formats are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers image-based PDF decks, PowerPoint workflows through companion tools, and LaTeX Beamer presentations.

faq.question: Is an API key required?
faq.answer: Only AI image generation requires an OpenRouter API key. Planning, templates, and local review guidance do not require it.

faq.question: Can I use confidential research figures?
faq.answer: Avoid uploading confidential material. Attached figures are sent to OpenRouter for generation and review.

faq.question: Does it create editable PowerPoint files directly?
faq.answer: It provides a PowerPoint workflow, but native PPTX creation relies on separate companion tools.

faq.question: How does presentation validation work?
faq.answer: Local scripts inspect slide counts, duration guidance, dimensions, fonts, file size, and Beamer compilation.

faq.question: What software dependencies are needed?
faq.answer: Requirements vary by workflow and may include Python libraries, OpenRouter access, pdflatex, PDF tools, or PowerPoint utilities.
